> Teaching story. Living project architecture for humans and review grounding. Not Typology seed evidence (see `evidence/typology/architecture_brief.md`).
Gitboard operates as a local coordination layer between forge APIs (GitHub/GitLab) and the developer's workstation. The system architecture is organized around two primary entrypoints (doors) and a set of synchronization jobs.
## Entrypoints
The CLI (Sync Door): The `gitboard` command-line interface acts as the primary driver for state acquisition. It orchestrates the interaction with `gh`, `glab`, and `git` to pull remote status and local worktree metadata into the local environment.
The Web Server (View Door): The `serve` command launches a local web server that provides a visual dashboard. This entrypoint transforms the synchronized local state into a human-readable interface for monitoring CI status, open MRs, and failed jobs.
## Objective Ledger Jobs
The system's activity is defined by the following functional objectives:
Forge Synchronization: Periodically querying forge APIs to update the local view of remote repository states, including MR status and CI pipelines.
Local State Integration: Mapping remote forge data to the local filesystem and worktree state, enabling the "local code-change board" capability.
Dashboard Rendering: Serving the processed local state via HTTP to the user's browser for real-time triage and monitoring.
